beats.narration_en: Engineers built this road to make your car shake on purpose.
Look beside the white line, these are shallow cuts, not bumps piled onto the road.
A tire crosses one dip, then another, that repeated contact creates sound and vibration.
Now the strange shaking makes sense, the tire has reached the shoulder outside the travel lane.
The noise and vibration can alert a distracted or drowsy driver to that drift.
But the road cannot steer, that warning still needs a driver who notices and responds.
Those cuts beside the road are supposed to make noise, they are a warning system.
From above, you see a stripe of grooves, from the side, you see cuts below the surface.
Each dip changes the tire's contact with the road, repeat that, and you get a rumble.
The important part is where it happens: beside the white edge line, on the shoulder.
The sound and vibration can tell a distracted driver that the car has drifted out of its lane.
So these grooves do not drive the car, they warn the person who still controls it.
A sudden rumble could be the road trying to tell you something.
Follow the tire past the white edge line, it has reached shallow cuts in the shoulder.
A tire dips into each cut, creating repeated contact that produces sound and vibration.
That turns a quiet drift into a warning you can hear and feel inside the car.
It can help a distracted or drowsy driver notice what happened, it cannot guarantee a response.
The rumble answers the mystery: you reached the shoulder, the driver still has to notice and react.
